title: End-to-end evidence for independent task releases
outcomes: Two different task profiles deliver ordered independent releases with durable proof and an honest separate live runtime receipt.

in: Reusable local Git remote campaign, rejected critic/repair and dependency ordering, failure/property regressions, small live Codex worker run
boundaries: Disposable campaign repository and local bare remote; canonical source .go remains separate; supported managed native CLI path

decision_rights: Authorize execution and choose model; GO on 2026-09-13
Implement bounded contract choices and document compatibility behavior

constraints: Use the shipped lifecycle primitives; test doubles must exercise actual subprocess/verification/Git/readback boundaries.
Different model/effort profiles and required release dependency are explicit. Failed or missing release proof must prevent the next claim.
Reuse focused existing regressions for crash/effect/cleanup boundaries and add cross-task campaign/completeness/state-roundtrip coverage; no copied fake implementation.
Live proof uses available Terra High and Astra Medium as requested by task; preserve raw results and mark access failure as a real proof blocker. Never replace a failed live run with fixture claims.
A worktree is a Git organization mechanism, not a security or dependency/test-environment isolation boundary.
No GitHub Actions, global skills edits or production targets.

quality_attributes.measure: Second claim before first required release

quality_attributes.scenario: Fail critic or mutate verified state
quality_attributes.measure: Untested content marked released or done
Lost proof or duplicate confirmed effects

quality_attributes.scenario: Run real native models separately from fixtures

risks: Live runtime access may fail despite model catalog availability.
Local bare remote proves Git release/readback, not an external deployment provider.
